text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock was essentially flat today, rising just 0.28%, as oil markets cooled on cautious optimism about Middle East diplomacy. Crude prices fell on October 20th after traders began hoping for diplomatic progress to ease tensions in the region, even as attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continue. That price decline took some steam out of the refining sector — Marathon is sensitive to oil costs and fuel margins — which had surged earlier in the week when geopolitical tensions spiked oil above $109 per barrel.

The stock is up 9.87% over the past two weeks, reflecting a sharp rally driven by the escalation of Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Russian facilities that pushed crude prices higher. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity and fuel inventories remain moderate, meaning the company stands to benefit if crude stays elevated, but today's diplomatic glimmer trimmed some of that recent gain.
